titulo: Futuro perfecto and probability: Guesses: present and recent past

aula.objetivo: Form the futuro perfecto («habré terminado») to say what will already be finished by a future moment, and use it together with the simple future to make guesses about the present and the recent past («habrá llegado ya»).

itens.pt: to arrive late, to be late

blocos.titulo: I wonder…, he must have…: guessing with the future
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the future isn't only for what will happen. Spanish also uses it to GUESS about right now: «Pablo estará en casa» means "Pablo is probably at home" / "Pablo must be at home". STEP 2: the same goes for questions: «¿Dónde estará Pablo?» means "I wonder where Pablo is". English needs "I wonder"; Spanish just puts the verb in the future. As an old grammar for English speakers puts it, "to wonder" is often best translated by the future of probability: "Has he come yet, I wonder?" = «¿Habrá venido ya?», "I wonder who that man is" = «¿Quién será ese hombre?». STEP 3: to guess about something that has just happened, use the futuro perfecto: «Habrá llegado ya» (he must have arrived by now), «¿Habrá perdido el autobús?» (I wonder if he missed the bus). STEP 4: notice the difference in certainty. «Ha llegado» states a fact. «Habrá llegado» is a guess — like English "he'll have arrived by now". STEP 5: the guess can be negative: «No habrá visto el mensaje» (he probably hasn't seen the message). STEP 6: an alternative is «deber de» + infinitive, like English "must": «Debe de estar en casa» (he must be at home), «Debe de haber llegado» (he must have arrived). In speech many people drop the «de» with the same meaning; be careful, because «debes hacerlo» without «de» is an obligation ("you must do it"). STEP 7: for a guess about a more distant past, Spanish uses the conditional: «Entonces tendría unos veinte años» (he must have been about twenty then). You only need to recognise it. STEP 8: words like «seguramente», «probablemente» and «supongo que» reinforce the guess.
blocos.comparacao: English needs extra words to guess: "I wonder where he is", "he must have missed the bus", "he's probably at home". Spanish simply uses the future: «¿Dónde estará?», «Habrá perdido el autobús», «Estará en casa». English "must" splits in two: «deber de» for a guess, «deber» (no «de») for an obligation.

erros.errado: Me pregunto si ha llegado ya.
erros.motivo: "I wonder if…" is correct but heavy; the natural Spanish guess is just the futuro perfecto.
To guess about right now, use the future. The conditional guesses about the past.
For an obligation, use «deber» without «de»; «deber de» is a guess.

blocos.enunciado: Imagine a friend hasn't turned up to meet you. Make five guesses out loud: «Habrá perdido el autobús. Estará en camino. No habrá oído el despertador…»
Conjugate «habré salido» in all six persons. Then say two sentences out loud with «para entonces» or «antes de las ocho».
